pending_commit.commit_message: vm_tools: concierge: Add ability to export a VM disk Add an export_disk option to concierge_client. This will allow a VM disk image to be moved to a location the user can access it. By default, copy the disk to Downloads. Allow a removable storage location to be specified instead. CQ-DEPEND=CL:1134042 BUG=none TEST=This exports to an SD CARD: concierge_client --export_disk --name=termina \ --cryptohome_id=5c8dd039b72b26f4f849d4654ba31d47172c3d04 --removable_media="SD Card" --export_name="huge_backup" And this puts the file in Downloads: concierge_client --export_disk --name=termina \ --cryptohome_id=5c8dd039b72b26f4f849d4654ba31d47172c3d04 --export_name="huge_backup" Change-Id: I23d9bbaa2c53af3f3ec0eea32d8f31c7c42dd9d1 Signed-off-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1134044 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Reviewed-by: Stephen Barber <smbarber@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

crosh: Allow 'vmc' to export VM images Plumb up the export_disk client command so it can be used from crosh. There is a known issue where external storage devices with spaces in the name don't work because of the lack of command line parsing. BUG=none TEST=The following puts a disk image in Downloads. vmc export termina dl_backup Once completed, dl_backup.qcow2 will be visible from the files app. And adding a third argument specifies the name of a removable media device to save to: vmc export termina sd_backup sdcard this will copy the file to /media/removable/sdcard Change-Id: I7bb0e5aa69f5bc28603639928304abf6f145fc5c Signed-off-by: Dylan Reid <dgreid@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1134045 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org>

vm_tools: concierge: Remove useless parent checks Because we now base 64 encode the passed in file name, there is no way for it to reference its parent. sys-apps: usbguard: Enable usbguard by installing upstart config. Usbguard is a system daemon that allows whitelisting usb devices with a configurable policy. This commit enables the init logic needed to prevent new USB devices from being connected when a device is locked while still allowing devices that were connected when Chrome OS was locked. CQ-DEPEND=CL:1114119 BUG=None TEST=Check that the usbguard-daemon works at the lockscreen. CHROMIUM: config: normalize config This runs: ./chromeos/scripts/kernelconfig olddefconfig Here's an explanation of what we see here: CONFIG_DRM_EVDI was turned on in CL:1084988 ("drm/evdi: Add evdi module build config"). That change wasn't properly normalized. As you can see in CL:1084987 this causes the following configs to be turned on: + select FB_SYS_FILLRECT + select FB_SYS_COPYAREA + select FB_SYS_IMAGEBLIT + select DRM_KMS_HELPER + select DRM_KMS_FB_HELPER FB_SYS_FOPS, FB_CFB_FILLRECT, FB_CFB_COPYAREA, FB_CFB_IMAGEBLIT, and FB_DEFERRED_IO are selected by DRM_KMS_FB_HELPER. BUG=None TEST=None Change-Id: I62bad724198d1b17e61bc16c6b9d570c78fd4b7a Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1135724 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

Un-deprecate supervision_transition field. Child accounts can graduate from supervision, however we must only trigger graduation flow when there was a transition from child to regular. Otherwise, we'll affect other managed user types, which may also exit management. These bits are sent during boot instead of via a mojo IPC, so we can avoid making blocking mojo calls from Android on every startup to obtain that information. BUG=chromium:836246 TEST=no Change-Id: I16c85dde6ec8a2880ba8c3549826af9448308aa7 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1129700 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: Patricia Hongo <phongo@google.com> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>
